title: Cottrell's collapsible bass drum
summary: Frazier describes the folding bass drum, its case, heads and rigging, and that he saw only Cottrell use one.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Did you ever see that folding drum he had?
Yeah, the collapsible. What was that like, that collapsible? Well, it was one of the reminders, the way they used to fold it, they had a case similar like the old-time baritone saxophone case.
Yeah.
And used to dampen it. When you dampen the head, you always had to put a piece of newspaper when you dampen it, and to stop the head from getting dry rot.
Oh yeah.

See, every time you close the bass drum, you take a piece of newspaper and you dampen it, and you put it between the seam of the drum, then you fold it over. Oh yeah, yeah, yeah. It's like you do a seal.
Yeah.
Then you stick. But the case of the bass drum looked just like a baritone cypher. It was like a steeple, like a humpback to it.
It was the actual drum, bass drum that folded up small.

Yeah, it folded, yeah. It took plenty of time to rig it up, but it was not quite wide as this bass drum. After it'd be folded, I figured this would be about the width of about 12, 1 foot, 12 inches after it'd be rigged up. Yeah. You understand? It'd be about 1 foot.
And then that would fold up and it'd go in a separate case, a separate case.
A separate case, that's right. It's similar to these old-time baritone saxophone cases.
Do you remember how many times it folded? Did they fold it in half?
Just twice. Just one fold over. It was like you take a sheet of paper, like in a diamond shape.
Like so, like that.
Like so, like that. Just make one fold over, you see. Then you had all your rods and all. You had to put all that together.
Do you remember what the drum was made of?
It was sort of a lumen-like. Oh yeah. Like a metal. But it had no more calf heads. Normal calf skin heads, that's right. Two heads. Two heads. Normal calf skin heads.
How about the tuning stuff?
Well, the rods used to go, all that. He fixed, you know, you could call it collapsible drums.
Yeah.
After he put them and he'd add the rods and all that to it, it took a little time, you know, to rig them up.
But you've never seen anybody else with that.
He's the only one I've seen with that.
You know where he got that drum from?
No, I wouldn't know. Some say now he's out of Chicago. I wouldn't, I wouldn't, I would not, would not show about that, you know.
I guess you don't remember what make it was.
No, I really wouldn't know what make the drum it was. But he's the first I've seen with it.
Yeah.
Around in New Orleans.
